OR

"… saw the destruction of the building, resulting in [DATA EXPUNGED] eventually being contained by Mobile Task Forces…"

Depending on the nature of the expunged data.

item.content:encoded:
This is a great SCP, and I get the broad-strokes picture, but I'm having a little difficulty picturing how the details work. Like, how did things go down in the universe immediately BEFORE the universe where the researchers are all actively being killed? Why were they continuing with the experiment at all? "Okay, the rover's checked out and ready to go, let's just open the door and send it thr-Oh! Weird, through this door immediately next to me, another version of myself is being shot and killed. Should we maybe abort the experiment, put something heavy in front of the door, and leave a sign for other extrauniversal rovers explaining the danger and asking them to turn around? …Nah, you know what, let's just see where this goes."
Someone already suggested the possibility of networking your computer with a computer on both sides to make an infinite network, but given that this is the SCP universe, I could see that leading to all sorts of bad scenarios. However, they could have gotten more comprehensive data than they got from the rover experiment without even interacting with any universes except those immediately adjacent to theirs in either direction. Just make a video where you travel from the left door to the right door in your OWN universe. If the universe in either direction can't participate in this experiment with you (incompatible data formats, clear and present danger, etc.), include yourself explaining why that is the case in your video. Copy it to two portable hard drives, and swap drives with the universe on each side. Scan for hazards, save locally, then overwrite the contents of each portable drive with the data that was previously on the other portable drive. Return drives to original owners, and make sure you get your original drives back (but now with new data on them). Check for hazards, save locally, put contents of each drive on the other drive, repeat until hazard detected or local storage full. Splice together videos from the left side in reverse of the order that you got them, then your own video, then the videos from the right side in the same order that you got them. Assuming you explain the procedure to each adjacent non-hazardous universe (that didn't already come up with it on their own), you'd all end up with the same video of the leftmost compatible researcher explaining why they can't go farther left, then continuous travel from left to right, ending with the rightmost compatible researcher explaining why they can't go farther right.

item.content:encoded:
I actually like experiment log 3 way, way more than log 4. "Go through alternate universes, see everyone dead and/or maimed and/or eldritchated" is what I expected and what's been here before. The heart of the article, I think, is experiment 3, where this bizarre and inexplicable dimensional tunnel just creates a series of entirely mundane problems — no, not even mundane problems, mundane HASSLES, and across an infinite brane of multiverses an infinite number of doctors and scientists and technicians are throwing up their hands in frustration and saying "Ugh, this shit again!" They get into fights over sporting events and yell at their own alternate versions for holding things up because SOME of our universes got shit to do today and poor, poor D-970-296-1 keeps getting jumped until someone hangs a sign on him saying "quit jumping this dude". That juxtaposition of the supernatural phenomenon and the completely mundane irritants that arise from it is great.

I feel like Experiment 4 driving everyone to varying degrees of breakdown after seeing Horrible Things From The Video kind of undermines that unique feeling. Maybe I'm the only one that likes 3 this much more than 4, but maybe I'm not. My unsolicited advice/request would be to change the log of experiment 4 and make it feel more like "as we get further from our universe, differences are more pronounced and threatening, but the occupants appear to be just as irritated by just as mundane of crap." The universe the probe runs by where the research team is under attack — maybe they are under attack by the research team from an adjacent universe, and they're just screaming petty and personal insults at each other, because they really pissed each other off. One of the iterations is so strange that any living things that pass into it from more than 50 iterations away are driven mad; the residents of this iteration hang a sign in their doorway warning other universes of this, and request they stop sending guys over because they make a huge mess. The procession of automated probes passing by from the other universes "behind" them on the helix seem to get slowly rustier, bloodier, more Silent Hill-ey, until there's a long string of them that appear to be made entirely out of ground meat and leave trails of blood and ichor in their tire tracks… and then a few probes after that, someone hastily duct-taped a couple of squeegee mops to the front of the probe to soak up the gross mess those meat universe guys think it's okay to leave in everyone else's hall. That sort of thing.
